entry.title: 2026 Hyundai Motor Group Tech Talent Forum | Hyundai News

media:group.media:title: 2026 Hyundai Motor Group Tech Talent Forum | Hyundai News
media:group.media:description:
What does it take to turn disruption into opportunity and build a company that reaches far beyond cars?
Hyundai Motor Company President and CEO José Muñoz shares how the group is navigating a changing global market while expanding across electrification, robotics, autonomous mobility, AI, hydrogen and advanced manufacturing. He highlights Hyundai’s global growth, ambitious product plans through 2030, partnerships with companies including Waymo, Amazon and NVIDIA, and a vision of technology guided by “Progress for Humanity.”
Muñoz also explains why people are central to the company’s culture and reflects on Hyundai Hope On Wheels and its work supporting pediatric cancer research. His message: keep trying, adapt to challenges and turn crises into opportunities to do better.

FAQ
Q: What is Hyundai Motor Group’s Autonomous Vehicle (AV) Foundry strategy with Waymo? A: Hyundai is serving as an autonomous vehicle foundry by manufacturing tens of thousands of purpose-built Waymo robotaxis based on the Ioniq 5 electric vehicle platform at the HMGMA facility in Bryan County, Georgia, integrated alongside a multi-billion-dollar partnership with NVIDIA.
Q: When will Hyundai deploy Boston Dynamics Atlas humanoid robots in manufacturing? A: Hyundai Motor Group will begin deploying Boston Dynamics Atlas humanoid robots at the HMGMA Georgia smart factory in 2028 for parts sequencing and repetitive logistics, targeting a scaling capacity of at least 30,000 units by 2030.
Q: What is Hyundai's extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) and what is its targeted driving range? A: Hyundai's next-generation EREV platform combines an electric powertrain with an onboard internal combustion generator to achieve a targeted continuous driving range exceeding 600 miles (over 1,000 km) without stopping to recharge.
Q: Where does Hyundai Motor Group rank in global automotive sales and profitability? A: Hyundai Motor Group ranks as the world's third-largest automotive group by global sales volume and the second-most profitable automaker globally, having overtaken Volkswagen in global operating income.
Q: How fast did Genesis reach the 1 million sales milestone compared to other luxury brands? A: Genesis achieved 1 million cumulative sales in seven years and eight months—reaching the milestone faster than any standalone luxury automotive brand in history, including Lexus and Tesla.
Q: How does Hyundai sell vehicles on Amazon? A: Through an exclusive automotive retail partnership, Hyundai enables consumers to search inventory, configure financing, and complete vehicle purchases directly on Amazon, broadening brand discovery beyond traditional OEM dealership portals.
Q: What is Hyundai Hope On Wheels and what is its impact? A: Founded over 26 years ago by Hyundai Motor America and its U.S. dealers, Hyundai Hope On Wheels has committed over $300 million to pediatric cancer research across 25 leading medical institutions, helping raise childhood cancer survival rates from 75% to over 85%.

media:group.media:title: 2027 Hyundai TUCSON Features Reveal | Hyundai News
media:group.media:description:
Take a guided tour of the key features of the all-new TUCSON, Hyundai’s best-selling vehicle, with Senior Vice President Product & Mobility Olabisi Boyle. Learn how Hyundai developed the bold design for the fifth-generation TUCSON SUV, to achieve class-leading interior volume. Boyle explains how the design team enhanced real-world usability, pointing out all the small design changes designed to improve the lives of drivers and passengers.
00:00 - Introduction: Olabisi Boyle & Fifth-Gen 2027 Tucson Overview 00:10 - Total Interior Volume (153.6 Cu. Ft.) & Exterior Growth Dimensions 00:48 - Rear Seat Legroom, Phone Storage & Car Seat Practicality 01:23 - Cargo Hold & Open-Source Third-Party Storage Accessory Points 01:52 - Driver Ergonomics: Physical Buttons & "Muscle Memory" Controls 02:09 - Column Shifter, Dual Wireless Charging & 100W USB-C Laptop Port 02:34 - Segment-Leading 17-Inch Infotainment Screen & Vehicle Status Alerts 02:55 - Powertrain Freedom: ICE Gas vs. Next-Gen Hybrid Customer Choice
FAQ
Q: Does the 2027 Hyundai Tucson have physical buttons for climate control? A: Yes. Hyundai intentionally kept dedicated physical buttons and rotary dials for volume, tuning, climate control mode, and fan speed. As Olabisi Boyle explains, drivers adjusting temperatures in traffic rely on muscle memory, and "you cannot build muscle memory on a menu."
Q: What is the screen size of the 2027 Hyundai Tucson head unit? A: The 2027 Tucson features a segment-leading 17-inch center infotainment head unit display, designed to deliver high visibility for navigation, media, and vehicle status alerts (such as open door indicators).
Q: What is the total interior volume of the fifth-generation 2027 Tucson? A: The all-new 2027 Tucson delivers a class-leading 153.6 cubic feet of total interior volume. The vehicle grew by 2.4 inches in overall length and 1.6 inches in width, translating into expanded rear passenger legroom and headroom.
Q: What are the open-source points in the 2027 Tucson cargo space? A: Hyundai engineered dedicated open-source mounting points in the rear cargo area to allow third-party developers and owners to create custom storage solutions, dividers, and modular accessories over the lifetime of the SUV.
Q: What charging ports and console features are in the 2027 Tucson? A: Moving the gear shift to the steering column freed up the center console to include two wireless charging pads side-by-side, two full-size cup holders, multi-level storage, and a high-power 100-watt USB-C port capable of charging a laptop.
Q: What powertrain choices are available for the 2027 Tucson? A: Hyundai offers both traditional internal combustion engine (ICE) gasoline and next-generation Hybrid powertrains, ensuring customers have the freedom to choose the drive system that fits their lifestyle.

00:00 - Introduction: Simon Loasby & The 2027 Hyundai Tucson Vision 00:12 - Exterior Silhouette: Taller Stance & Upgraded SUV Proportions 00:39 - Architectural Front Lighting: Indirect H-Graphic DRLs 01:10 - Side Profile: Longer Wheelbase & Class-Leading Interior Room 01:31 - Art of Steel Design Language: Stretched Steel Tension 01:53 - Interior Architecture: Furnished Space Ergonomics & Dual Storage 02:24 - Floating Armrest: Ergonomic Display Support & Glasses Storage 02:37 - Stretched Steel Fenders: Advanced Press Forming Engineering 02:50 - Prism Rear Lamp: Aerodynamic Tail Lens & Edge H-Lighting 03:28 - Extended Rear Door Opening: 83-Degree Family Practicality & Car Seats 03:54 - Rear Cabin Comfort: Class-Leading Legroom & Utility Amenities 04:22 - Conclusion: The All-New 2027 Hyundai Tucson Walkaround
FAQ
Q: Who designed the all-new 2027 Hyundai TUCSON? A: The exterior and interior design of the fifth-generation 2027 Hyundai TUCSON was led by Simon Loasby, Senior Vice President and Head of the Hyundai Design Center.
Q: What is Hyundai's "Art of Steel" design language on the new TUCSON? A: "Art of Steel" is Hyundai’s exterior design philosophy that stretches automotive steel to its physical limits. It features volumetric stamped panels, sharp muscular tension across the body sides, and oversized front and rear fenders that create high-contrast light and shadow surfaces.
Q: How much wider does the 2027 Hyundai TUCSON rear door open? A: The 2027 TUCSON rear passenger doors open to 83 degrees—a full 10 degrees wider than the typical 70–75 degree industry standard. This wider aperture allows effortless passenger entry and makes loading rear-facing child car seats substantially easier.
Q: How does the 2027 TUCSON front and rear lighting work? A: Inspired by modern architectural lighting, the front features an illuminated horizontal element with indirect LED lighting creating an unmistakable "H" signature. The rear incorporates Hyundai's aerodynamic "Prism Lighting"—projecting light across a transparent void onto a matte rear surface to match the front H-edge light signature.
Q: What is the "Furnished Space" interior concept in the 2027 TUCSON? A: The "Furnished Space" cabin philosophy treats the interior like a set of refined, functional home furniture. It introduces a two-tier instrument panel for layered driver and passenger storage, moves the digital gauge cluster above the steering wheel to keep eyes on the road, and adds a dedicated floating palm-rest with integrated hidden glasses storage.
Q: Does the longer wheelbase of the 2027 TUCSON increase cabin space? A: Yes. The stretched wheelbase and increased overall length expand interior volume to class-leading dimensions, delivering superior second-row passenger legroom, abundant rear headroom, and door-integrated utility amenities including deep cupholders, smartphone pockets, and high-speed USB-C charging ports.

entry.title: The all-new TUCSON – The Boldest | World Premiere Highlights | Hyundai News

media:group.media:title: The all-new TUCSON – The Boldest | World Premiere Highlights | Hyundai News
media:group.media:description:
Join us for the world premiere of the all-new TUCSON, where Manhattan’s iconic skyline set the stage for an unforgettable evening. The journey began with a ferry ride across the East River, leading guests to a waterfront venue framed by “The Boldest TUCSON” typography. The night reached its peak with a bold reveal, as the standard model and the rugged XRT PRO drove out together in a powerful simultaneous debut.
Guests also enjoyed an up-close look at design sketches, Next-generation Hybrid System(Intelligent Efficiency), and Pleos Connect (Everyday Progress) in our exhibition space, alongside the stunning open-air vehicle display on the pier.
Relive the highlights of a night that celebrated the bold new era of Hyundai’s hero model. The Boldest TUCSON.
Discover more: https://www.hyundai.com/worldwide/en/suv/tucson-2026/highlights
FAQ
Q: Why is the United States the primary market for the 2027 Hyundai Tucson? A: The United States accounts for over 30% of Hyundai's global sales and remains the top priority market for the brand. The 2027 Tucson was specifically shaped to meet US customer demand for rugged design, advanced hybrid powertrains, and versatile interior space, while remaining a core global hero model sold on six continents.
Q: Where is the 2027 Hyundai Tucson Hybrid manufactured? A: For the first time, production of the Hyundai Tucson Hybrid is being brought directly to North America at Hyundai's manufacturing facility in Montgomery, Alabama. Global production will also continue at plants in South Korea and the Czech Republic to support international markets.
Q: What is Hyundai's EV and Hybrid strategy moving forward? A: Following market shifts, Hyundai adjusted its electrification strategy to offer a flexible range of powertrains—including Hybrids (HEV), Plug-In Hybrids (PHEV), Extended-Range Electric Vehicles (EREV), Battery Electric Vehicles (BEV), and Fuel Cell EVs (FCEV). By 2030, two-thirds of Hyundai's global sales will be electrified models, led by strong consumer demand for high-efficiency hybrids.
Q: What power and fuel economy stats does the 2027 Hyundai Tucson Hybrid deliver? A: The 2027 Tucson Hybrid delivers 233 horsepower (a 27% increase in power over the gasoline engine) and achieves up to 42 MPG, offering an optimal balance of fuel economy, instant acceleration, and all-wheel-drive capability for families.
Q: What is Pleos Connect and the Gleo AI assistant? A: Pleos Connect is Hyundai Motor Group’s software-defined vehicle (SDV) platform developed by 42dot. It introduces "Gleo" (or "Hyundai"), an in-vehicle native AI assistant powered by LLM technology that understands natural language, context, multi-zone seating commands, and complex conversational requests without requiring rigid voice prompts.
Q: How does Hyundai ensure long-term software updates for connected vehicles? A: Pleos Connect is integrated into the cloud, allowing natural language processing and software features to scale without overloading local vehicle hardware. This cloud infrastructure supports continuous Over-The-Air (OTA) updates, ensuring the vehicle receives new features and improved capabilities throughout its lifespan.
Q: What is Hyundai's outlook on Extended-Range Electric Vehicles (EREVs)? A: Hyundai is launching EREVs in the first half of next year for Hyundai and Genesis brands. Combining pure EV driving dynamics with an onboard generator, EREVs offer extended driving ranges exceeding 600 miles to eliminate range anxiety while charging infrastructure continues to expand.
Q: Why did Hyundai keep physical buttons inside the 2027 Tucson cabin? A: Following an "Eyes on the road, hands on the wheel" safety philosophy, Hyundai intentionally paired large digital touchscreen displays with physical buttons for frequently used controls (climate, volume, drive modes) so drivers can make adjustments by touch without taking their eyes off the road.

Q: What is the all-new 2027 Hyundai TUCSON’s Hybrid output and efficiency? A: Powered by a dual-motor hybrid setup (including a 47.7 kW drive motor), the 2027 TUCSON Hybrid delivers 233 combined horsepower, targets 42 MPG, reaches an upgraded 118 mph top speed, and offers up to 3,000 lbs of towing capacity.
Q: What is Stay Mode on the 2027 TUCSON? A: A segment-first feature, Stay Mode leverages Hyundai EV engineering to power the climate system and electronics for extended periods with the engine off, keeping the cabin comfortable without burning fuel.
Q: How much bigger is the all-new 2027 TUCSON? A: It is 2.4 inches longer, 1.6 inches wider, and features a 1.2-inch longer wheelbase. It offers a class-leading 41.7 cubic feet of rear cargo space, while rear doors swing open up to 83 degrees for easier entry and car-seat loading.
Q: What is the TUCSON XRT Pro? A: The XRT Pro is our rugged off-road trim equipped with +1.2 inches of ground clearance, all-terrain tires, front recovery hooks, and world-first Smart Terrain Assist that actively reads surface terrain to optimize wheel traction.
Q: What is Pleos Connect and Gleo AI? A: Developed by 42dot, Pleos Connect is our next-gen SDV platform. It integrates Gleo AI—a native LLM assistant capable of natural conversational requests, multi-command execution, and zone-specific cabin recognition.
Q: Does the 2027 TUCSON have physical buttons? A: Yes. Essential driving and climate controls (volume, tuning, fan, and temperature) remain physical buttons and rotary dials to support driver focus and muscle memory.
Q: Does the TUCSON support Over-The-Air (OTA) updates? A: Yes. Pleos Connect receives regular OTA software updates to continuously expand vehicle intelligence, apps, and features over time.
